# javaabu/widgets

> WordPress classic-style widgets for Laravel. A widget type is a PHP class extending Javaabu\Widgets\Widget: its settings are javaabu/stencil components, and it renders with a Blade view and a React component. Developers define locations (Widgets::location('sidebar', ...)), rendered with <x-widgets::location name="sidebar" /> or <WidgetLocation> from @javaabu/widgets. Admins add, order (keyboard-accessible drag and drop), configure and remove widgets on pages from Route::widgets(), in Blade or Inertia React. Permissions come from javaabu/permissions (view_widgets, edit_widgets, per-location). Settings marked ->translatable() are per language with javaabu/translatable. English and Dhivehi, RTL.

Paths are relative to this file. In a project, that's vendor/javaabu/widgets/.

## Rules

- Define locations and register widget types in a service provider's boot(): `Widgets::location('footer', fn () => __('Footer'))->allow([...])->max(3)`, `Widgets::register(MyWidget::class)`. Use closures for labels so they're translated per request.
- A widget extends `Javaabu\Widgets\Widget` with a static `key()` (never change it once saved), `name()`, `settings()` (stencil components with labels, rules and defaults), and optionally `data()`, `view()`, `component()` and `shouldRender()`. Don't put the wrapper <section> in the view: the location adds it.
- Read settings with `$widget->setting('key')` (current locale, defaults filled in). Don't read `$widget->settings` directly for display: translatable settings are stored as locale maps there.
- Render locations with `<x-widgets::location name="..." />` in Blade, and `<WidgetLocation name="..." widgets={...} />` in React with data from `Widgets::props([...])` or `Widgets::toArray('...')`. Never loop over WidgetInstance models in a view.
- Register a React component for every custom widget: `registerWidgets({ "recent-posts": RecentPosts })`. Keep its markup the same as the Blade view.
- Links in settings use the `SafeUrl` rule; render them through `Url::safe()` / `safeUrl()`.
- Register the admin routes yourself with `Route::widgets([...])` and the guard, prefix, name and middleware the app uses. Give roles `edit_widgets` (and location permissions), then run `php artisan permissions:sync`.
- Override behaviour by extending `WidgetsController` (config `widgets.controllers.widgets`) or `WidgetPolicy` (`widgets.policy`, `Gate::policy()`), not by copying routes.
- Pass every user-facing string through `__()` and add it to `lang/dv.json`.
